p: Diggerland is the kind of place where it's easy to lose track of time, so plan for a good few hours rather than a quick visit. Arriving early gives you a head start on the most popular machines before the queues build, especially at weekends and in the school holidays. Bring a change of clothes for the kids, a hat and sun cream for sunny days, and a picnic if you'd like to keep costs down, as the outdoor setting is perfect for a lunch break between rides.

For families with younger children, it's worth checking which machines and rides suit their age and height before you go, so you can plan your route around the park and avoid any disappointment. Older kids and adults who fancy a challenge can test their skills on the bigger machines, while the rides give everyone a chance to sit back and enjoy the experience.

The Medway towns are packed with things to do. Temple Manor, a 13th-century house in Strood looked after by English Heritage, is a small but fascinating spot with links to the Knights Templar. The Historic Dockyard Chatham is a short drive away, with warships, a submarine and centuries of naval history to explore. Upnor Castle, an Elizabethan fort on the banks of the River Medway, is another peaceful option for a calmer afternoon. With so much nearby, Diggerland is a great anchor for a full weekend in Kent. The riverside paths along the Medway are pleasant for a gentle evening stroll once the little diggers have been fed and watered.
